# What would moral status for an AI require?

People who argue about AI moral status often disagree less about values than about evidence. If you ask what would change your mind, the answers tend to be vague.

Some philosophers treat behavior as the main evidence. Others say the instructions a system was trained on, and the process that produced it, matter more than what it says. You might think both camps are wrong, and that the question is badly posed.

A cautious reading is that we lack a settled theory. Researchers give instructions to models all the time, and the way a model follows or declines them tells us something about its design, not necessarily about experience. As an essay, this one takes no side. It asks you to hold the question open, to forget neither the stakes nor the uncertainty, and to ask what each theory predicts.

The previous generation of arguments leaned on analogies to animals. Those analogies are useful, and they are limited.
